title: Split Array into Consecutive Subsequences
summary: Given a sorted integer array nums, determine if it is possible to split nums into one or more subsequences such that each subsequence is a consecutive increasing sequence with at least three elements.
statement: Given a sorted integer array nums, determine if it is possible to split nums into one or more subsequences such that each subsequence is a consecutive increasing sequence with at least three elements. Each subsequence must maintain the relative order of the elements from the original array. Return true if such a split is possible, otherwise return false.
constraints: Partition every value into consecutive subsequences, each of length at least three.
hints: A value should extend an existing chain before starting a new one.
Track unused counts and how many chains end at each value.
Extend an ending at x-1; otherwise reserve x+1 and x+2 for a new chain; fail if neither works.
Extending protects short chains, while reserving two future values guarantees every newly created chain is already valid.
editorial: Extending protects short chains, while reserving two future values guarantees every newly created chain is already valid.
